overview: Buitreraptor was a small unenlagiine dromaeosaurid theropod from the Late Cretaceous of Argentina, approximately 100–94 million years ago (Cenomanian), discovered in the Candeleros Formation of Río Negro Province. At about 1.3 metres in length, it was a rooster-sized predator with an unusually elongated, narrow skull bearing many small, unserrated teeth, suggesting dietary specialisation. Its name means 'Buitrera vulture roost plunderer', after the Buitrera locality.

Described by Makovicky, Apesteguía, and Agnolin in 2005, Buitreraptor is a pivotal taxon for understanding the biogeography of dromaeosaurids. Its assignment to Unenlagiinae—a Southern Hemisphere subclade that includes Unenlagia and Rahonavis—supports the hypothesis that dromaeosaurids colonised Gondwana separately from their Northern Hemisphere relatives, or that the group had a wider early distribution before Pangaea fragmented.

articles.title: Discovery and Naming
articles.body: Buitreraptor gonzalezorum was described in 2005 by Peter Makovicky, Sebastián Apesteguía, and Federico Agnolin from the Candeleros Formation of Río Negro Province, Argentina. The species name honours the González family who facilitated access to the fossil site. Multiple specimens were recovered from the Buitrera locality, making it one of the best-known Gondwanan dromaeosaurids.

articles.title: Anatomy and Dentition
articles.body: Buitreraptor had a notably elongated, flat snout with many small, recurved but unserrated teeth—unlike the serrated teeth typical of most dromaeosaurids. This dentition suggests dietary specialisation, possibly targeting fish, small vertebrates, or invertebrates rather than large prey. Its body was slender and lightweight, consistent with an agile pursuit predator.

articles.title: Gondwanan Biogeography
articles.body: The placement of Buitreraptor within Unenlagiinae, a clade otherwise known from South America and Madagascar, is significant for understanding theropod dispersal. The presence of unenlagiines in Cenomanian Argentina, when the southern continents were still partially connected or recently separated, suggests either a Gondwanan origin for dromaeosaurids or an early dispersal across land bridges. This challenges the view that all dromaeosaurids radiated exclusively from Laurasia.

articles.title: Palaeoecology
articles.body: The Candeleros Formation was a semi-arid floodplain environment during the Cenomanian, shared with large sauropods like Argentinosaurus and predators such as Giganotosaurus. Buitreraptor occupied a very different ecological niche as a small, agile predator, likely hunting alongside other small theropods and avoiding competition with the large carnivores.

record.description: Buitreraptor gonzalezorum was a small long-snouted unenlagiine dromaeosaurid from the Cenomanian Candeleros Formation of Patagonia. The holotype is a near-complete skeleton with a skull, and additional individuals clarify much of its postcranial anatomy.
facts: Its numerous small, unserrated teeth differ from the broad serrated teeth of many northern dromaeosaurids.
The teeth support small-prey feeding but do not identify a single specialised diet.
